overall: The AG found the School Committee violated the OML by omitting an anticipated executive session topic from the posted notice and by failing to record posting date and time on three bodies' notices; other topic-detail claims were rejected.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged the November 23, 2015 notice was not properly posted and lacked sufficient detail, including an executive session topic.
allegations.key_passage: Furthermore, the executive session topic listed on the official notice sufficiently identifies the statutory purpose and adequately describes the discussion held behind closed doors

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the open and executive session topics on the November 23, 2015 notice lacked sufficient specificity.
allegations.key_passage: We find  that the notice sufficiently describes both the open and executive session discussion topics such that the public had sufficient information to decide whether to attend the meeting.

allegations.summary: The posted website notice omitted an anticipated executive session topic (a complaint against the Committee), though the final bulletin-board version included it.
allegations.key_passage: For the reasons stated above, we find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to list an anticipated executive session topic on its November 23, 2015 meeting notice.

allegations.summary: Notices for the Committee, Finance Committee, and Grievance Committee meetings did not conspicuously record the date and time they were posted.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that all three Committees violated the Law in this regard.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged some topics on the notice were not actually discussed in executive session, so their sufficiency was questioned.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we decline to address the sufficiency of those topics.

allegations.summary: The request for further review added allegations not included in the original complaint filed with the Committee.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review the additional  allegations because they are  beyond the scope of the original complaint filed  with the public body.

remedy: Release the portion of the November 23, 2015 executive session minutes that discussed the omitted topic, along with any documents used during that discussion.
Comply immediately and in the future with the Open Meeting Law; future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
